description: Mercure redistransport: dispatch hot path, subscriber lifecycle (3-RT/4-RT load-testing signals), publish + XREADGROUP, history replay, errors, presence, and go-redis connection pool. Provisioned and locked (`editable: false`) — UI edits won't persist; fork via the dashboard menu's Save As for local experiments, or edit `redistransport/grafana/dashboards/transport.json` and re-provision.

panels.title: Transport version
panels.description: redistransport build version label from mercure_redis_build_info.

panels.title: Healthy
panels.description: mercure_redis_healthy: 1 = transport reaching backend, 0 = health_threshold consecutive PING failures (load-shedding engaged). Multi-backend: one cell per `backend_type`; if ANY selected backend is unhealthy, that cell shows 0.

panels.title: Stream length
panels.description: Current XLEN of the mercure stream. Capped by max_length / event_ttl trim.

panels.title: Consumer lag
panels.description: XINFO GROUPS lag — entries the consumer group has yet to read. -1 (non-deterministic group state) is clamped to 0 in the max so it doesn't dominate; a count of unknown-state nodes is the second series. Sustained non-zero on the max series is the primary backpressure signal. Filter `$instance` to localize which replica is lagging. If both series are absent the metric isn't being scraped — check Prometheus targets.

panels.title: Consumer pending
panels.description: PEL size — XREADGROUP'd messages not yet XACK'd. Sustained growth past xreadgroup_batch_size churn = reading but not dispatching+acking.

panels.title: Clock drift
panels.description: Hub clock — Redis clock at connect time. Sampled once at NewRedisTransport. Large drift breaks UUIDv7 → stream-ID seek (clockSkewMargin tuning).

panels.title: Dispatch duration p99 by shard
panels.description: Per-shard p99 of dispatch_duration_seconds. Load-testing 3-RT/4-RT pass criterion: p99 < 50 ms during ramp-down. Skew across shards = bad subscriber-ID hash.

panels.title: Shard balance (subscribers per shard)
panels.description: mercure_redis_shard_subscribers{shard} — should be balanced. Load-testing 4-RT pass criterion: max/min ratio ≤ 1.5.

panels.title: Dispatch duration (aggregated)
panels.description: Aggregated dispatch_duration_seconds p50, p99 across all shards. Load-testing 7-RT pass: msgpack p99 reduced ≥ 25 % vs json at ≥ 1k publishes/s.

panels.title: Subscribers matched per dispatch
panels.description: p50/p99 of dispatch_subscribers_matched. Whale-tenant signal: one tenant ≥ 30 % of total p99 = Phase 2 isolation trigger.

panels.title: Add subscriber duration
panels.description: p50/p99 of add_subscriber_duration_seconds. Load-testing ramp-up signal: p99 rising = t.mu contention or TLS backpressure.

panels.title: Remove subscriber duration
panels.description: p50/p99 of remove_subscriber_duration_seconds. Load-testing 3-RT ramp-down disconnect-avalanche signal — A15 trigger if p99 spikes here.

panels.title: Subscriber/publisher rate-limited
panels.description: Rate of add/remove + rate-limiter activations. Sustained subscriber_rate_limited > 0 during a deployment is the limiter absorbing a reconnect storm (8-RT pass).

panels.title: Subscribers lost by reason
panels.description: Stacked rate of subscribers_lost_total{reason}. history_replay_failed = 9-RT trigger; other reasons surface transport-initiated drops bypassing the normal RemoveSubscriber path.

panels.title: Publish duration
panels.description: p50/p99 of publish_duration_seconds. Load-testing 8-RT: must stay bounded — if it grows with stream length, the Lua publish script is O(n).

panels.title: XREADGROUP latency
panels.description: p50/p99 of xreadgroup_latency_seconds — round-trip from BLOCK to entry batch arriving.

panels.title: XREADGROUP batch size
panels.description: p50 of entries returned per XREADGROUP call. Load-testing 8-RT pass: p50 > 1.0 under load = Redis batching properly. Stuck at 1.0 = poll-limited (raise xread_count or lower xread_block).

panels.title: Publish payload size
panels.description: Per-event payload size in bytes after codec encoding (XADD message body). p50 / p99 over the rate interval. Pair against the Redis-server `Network throughput` panel (bytes/sec input) and `Publish duration` p99 to predict bandwidth scaling and to spot publish-latency regressions caused by payload-size shifts during load tests.

panels.title: History replay duration & concurrency
panels.description: p99 history_replay_duration_seconds (fleet-aggregate; per-replica triage by filtering `$instance`) + history_replay_concurrent gauge (per-instance). Load-testing 9-RT pass: concurrent stays ≤ historyReplayConcurrency cap.

panels.title: History replay fallback rate
panels.description: Rate of replays that fell through to Pass 2 (requested Last-Event-ID was past retention). Sustained non-zero = retention too tight for the reconnect window.

panels.title: History replay truncated rate
panels.description: Rate of replays cut short before delivering the full backlog (subscriber disconnected — for any reason — or buffer full). Sustained non-zero = reconnecting clients miss history (slow consumers or restart churn). Aggregate companion to the mercure.history.truncated span attribute.

panels.title: XREADGROUP errors by kind
panels.description: Load-testing critical signal. nogroup is transient; other / nogroup_recreate_failed are sustained concerns.

panels.title: Publish errors by kind
panels.description: Stacked rate of publish_errors_total{kind}.

panels.title: Operational errors
panels.description: Combined rate of zombie_gc_errors_total, ttl_cleanup_errors_total, presence_heartbeat_errors_total, presence_read_errors_total{kind}, stream_decode_errors_total{kind}, history_cursor_rejected_total.

panels.title: Pre-binding metric drops
panels.description: mercure_redis_pre_binding_metric_drops_total — running count of metric-emission attempts that landed before RegisterMetricsWith bound the collector. Non-zero means the late-binding window covered live traffic; bind metrics earlier in the lifecycle (direct API: WithPrometheusRegisterer; Caddy: parent metrics_registry threaded through bindTransportMetrics in Provision). Read-through CounterFunc, so the value is the running atomic total at scrape time. Fleet-aggregate (`sum by (backend_type)`); filter `$instance` to localize which replica is dropping. Binary alarm: any non-zero is the operator signal.

panels.title: Presence payload bytes
panels.description: p50/p99 of presence_payload_bytes — size of presence SET serialized to Redis. Above presenceDetailThreshold (default 10k subscribers per node) the codec switches to summary mode.

panels.title: Presence read skipped
panels.description: Rate of per-key skips during GetSubscribers SCAN (key expired mid-scan or empty value). Steady-state non-zero is normal; sudden correlated drop in subscriber count + jump here = transport eviction event.

panels.title: Operations per second (hot paths)
panels.description: Throughput across hot paths via histogram _count derivatives. Pair with the duration p99 panels to spot latency degradation under load (8-RT publisher-rate ceiling: dispatch p99 < 50ms at target rate; correlate target rate here with Panel 9).

panels.title: Pool connections
panels.description: Per-instance go-redis client pool: total connections vs idle, one pair of lines per replica. A line approaching configured PoolSize = pressure on that replica (raise pool or shed load); single hot replica is visible without filtering.

panels.title: Pool timeouts
panels.description: Rate of pool acquisition timeouts. Load-testing 7-RT/8-RT critical signal: must stay 0. Non-zero rate = Redis I/O saturating before the transport — tune go-redis PoolSize.

panels.title: Pool hits / misses / stale
panels.description: go-redis pool acquisition outcomes. Hit = reused; miss = new conn opened; stale = idle conn discarded by health check.

panels.title: Server-side (redis_exporter sidecar — NOT filtered by Backend type)
Memory used vs max
panels.description: Server-side memory usage (redis_memory_used_bytes) versus the configured max (redis_memory_max_bytes). When `used` approaches `max`, the next write under `maxmemory-policy` triggers evictions or `OOM command not allowed`. `max=0` means the server has no maxmemory configured (Redis grows until host OOM).

panels.title: Evictions / rejected connections
panels.description: Evictions/sec = keys dropped by `maxmemory-policy` (LRU/LFU). Rejected/sec = clients turned away because `maxclients` was reached. Either signal correlates with hub-side dispatch p99 spikes; helps disambiguate transport-layer pressure from server-layer pressure.

panels.title: Commands per second
panels.description: Server-side command throughput (`info commandstats` aggregate). Hub publish/dispatch volume should track this — large divergence indicates a non-hub Redis client (operator session, exporter, or a second hub on the same instance).

panels.title: Connected clients
panels.description: Total clients on the Redis instance. Compare against the hub's `mercure_redis_client_pool_total_conns` (one line per hub replica — sum them mentally for the fleet-wide pool footprint) plus the Redis Exporter itself (~1 persistent connection) and any operator sessions. Sudden drops correlate with network blips or `maxclients` saturation.

panels.title: Keyspace hit ratio
panels.description: hits / (hits + misses). Streams (XADD/XREADGROUP) don't drive keyspace_hits/misses — only the presence GET/SCAN reads and the `:lastEventID` GET do. Sustained low ratio under steady load can indicate presence-key churn faster than `presence_ttl` (writes are SET-with-EX, one-shot — no separate EXPIRE).

panels.title: Slow log length
panels.description: Current entries in `SLOWLOG` (commands above `slowlog-log-slower-than` µs). Growing length means commands are crossing the slow threshold — often Lua publish, large XRANGE history replays, or contended SCAN passes. Pair with hub-side dispatch p99 to triage.

panels.title: Network throughput
panels.description: Bytes/sec read from and written to clients by the Redis server. Pair against hub-side dispatch throughput to spot fan-out amplification (output » input is normal during fan-out; sustained input bursts often track publish storms).

panels.title: CPU usage
panels.description: CPU seconds per wall-clock second consumed by the Redis server. Default Redis is single-threaded — 100% (one core) on `user` is full saturation; with `io-threads N` enabled the saturation point scales by N. `user` is application work (publish Lua, XREADGROUP, XADD); `sys` is kernel time (network, I/O). Sustained 70%+ on a single-threaded server (or 70% × `io-threads` count) means Redis is the bottleneck — correlate with publish/dispatch p99 spikes.

panels.title: Top 5 commands by avg latency
panels.description: Per-command average latency in seconds. Sourced from Redis `INFO commandstats` (cmdstat_*). Watch `evalsha` for Lua publish slowdowns and `xrange`/`xreadgroup` for history-replay or listener stalls. Note: `topk` is evaluated per scrape step, so the legend over a long window is the union of step-level top-5 sets — multi-select to focus.

panels.title: Memory fragmentation
panels.description: RSS / used ratio. 1.0 = no fragmentation. ~1.0–1.5 is normal steady state. Sustained > 1.5 with churn is allocator fragmentation pressure (rapid alloc/free of variably-sized stream entries during load tests). Combined with `redis_memory_used_rss_bytes` for the absolute RSS overshoot relative to `redis_memory_used_bytes` — sets the headroom needed beyond `maxmemory` to avoid OS-level OOM.

panels.title: Consumer groups attached to stream
panels.description: Number of consumer groups on the stream (XINFO GROUPS length, one group per hub instance plus any zombies not yet GC'd). Gates the misconfiguration alert: publishes succeed but no hub reads (groups == 0 while publish_rate > 0). Sentinel -1 means XINFO returned an error — distinct from 'Redis returned zero groups'.

panels.title: Available history window
panels.description: Wall-clock seconds between the stream's first and last entries (Redis-stamped <ms>-<seq>). Proactive companion to `history_replay_fallback_total`: alert when this falls below the expected client reconnect duration to catch retention-too-tight regressions BEFORE clients miss on reconnect. 0 on empty stream, -1 if entry IDs cannot be parsed.

panels.title: Zero-match dispatch rate (fan-out without consumers)
panels.description: Rate of XREADGROUP'd events that fanned out to zero local subscribers on this replica. Fleet-wide cost is this rate × replica count. Sustained non-zero often points at a publisher emitting to dead topics (heartbeats with no debug UI attached, retired subscription IDs, etc.).

panels.title: Per-instance p99 outliers (min 100 samples/window)
panels.description: Companion to the fleet-aggregate histogram panels above. Each row is a {instance, metric} pair whose sample count over the dashboard's `$__rate_interval` exceeds 100 (`increase(_count[$__rate_interval]) > 100`) — the minimum for stable p99 inference. Without this gate, low-traffic replicas would publish NaN-or-misleading p99s and dominate the top-K. Sort by Value column to find replicas drifting from fleet median. Use $instance template to drill into a specific replica's full histograms above.

targets.expr: label_replace(histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (instance, backend_type, le) (rate(mercure_redis_dispatch_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job",backend_type=~"$backend_type",instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval]))) and on (instance, backend_type) (sum by (instance, backend_type) (increase(mercure_redis_dispatch_duration_seconds_count{job=~"$job",backend_type=~"$backend_type",instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])) > 100), "metric", "dispatch_duration", "__name__", ".*")

label_replace(histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (instance, backend_type, le) (rate(mercure_redis_xreadgroup_latency_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job",backend_type=~"$backend_type",instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval]))) and on (instance, backend_type) (sum by (instance, backend_type) (increase(mercure_redis_xreadgroup_latency_seconds_count{job=~"$job",backend_type=~"$backend_type",instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])) > 100), "metric", "xreadgroup_latency", "__name__", ".*")

label_replace(histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (instance, backend_type, le) (rate(mercure_redis_history_replay_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job",backend_type=~"$backend_type",instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval]))) and on (instance, backend_type) (sum by (instance, backend_type) (increase(mercure_redis_history_replay_duration_seconds_count{job=~"$job",backend_type=~"$backend_type",instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])) > 100), "metric", "history_replay_duration", "__name__", ".*")

label_replace(histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (instance, backend_type, le) (rate(mercure_redis_publish_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job",backend_type=~"$backend_type",instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval]))) and on (instance, backend_type) (sum by (instance, backend_type) (increase(mercure_redis_publish_duration_seconds_count{job=~"$job",backend_type=~"$backend_type",instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])) > 100), "metric", "publish_duration", "__name__", ".*")

label_replace(histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (instance, backend_type, le) (rate(mercure_redis_add_subscriber_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job",backend_type=~"$backend_type",instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval]))) and on (instance, backend_type) (sum by (instance, backend_type) (increase(mercure_redis_add_subscriber_duration_seconds_count{job=~"$job",backend_type=~"$backend_type",instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])) > 100), "metric", "add_subscriber_duration", "__name__", ".*")

label_replace(histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (instance, backend_type, le) (rate(mercure_redis_remove_subscriber_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job",backend_type=~"$backend_type",instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval]))) and on (instance, backend_type) (sum by (instance, backend_type) (increase(mercure_redis_remove_subscriber_duration_seconds_count{job=~"$job",backend_type=~"$backend_type",instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])) > 100), "metric", "remove_subscriber_duration", "__name__", ".*")

panels.title: Subscribers shed by admission gate (rate/sec)
panels.description: New subscribers shed by the admission gate, by reason (rate = over the per-task accept-rate token bucket; capacity = over the concurrent-count ceiling). Non-zero = the hub is returning 429 at the front door. Headline signal for subscriber_rate_limit / subscriber_max_count.

panels.title: Presence reads capped (rate/sec)
panels.description: GetSubscribers calls refused (503) because the subscriber count exceeded subscriptions_max_subscribers — the presence-read memory guard. Non-zero = presence reads are being capped to protect task memory.

list.name: datasource
list.description: Prometheus datasource (matches the uid provisioned by `redistransport/grafana/datasources.yml`). Required so the dashboard imports cleanly into Grafana instances whose Prometheus datasource has a different uid.
list.label: Data source

list.name: job
list.description: Prometheus scrape job for Mercure hub instances, sourced from `mercure_redis_build_info`. If empty, the hub is not being scraped — check Prometheus targets, not this dashboard.
list.label: Job

list.name: instance
list.description: Hub pod/replica identifier (Prometheus `instance` label). Use to scope panels to a single replica during incident triage; leave on `All` for fleet-wide views.
list.label: Instance

list.name: backend_type
list.description: Detected backend server family (redis/valkey/unknown) sourced from `mercure_redis_build_info`. If empty, either the metric is not being scraped, OR the selected `$instance` runs Bolt/Local (no redistransport) — check Prometheus targets first, then check the transport in use.
list.label: Backend type
